newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEAH AND BAGGIO LIFT AC MILAN TO TOP OF TABLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH AND BAGGIO LIFT AC MILAN TO TOP OF TABLE.

text.p: George Weah scored twice and Roberto Baggio added a third as 10-man AC Milan thrashed Perugia 3-0 to move -- temporarily at least -- to the top of the Italian league on Sunday.
The champions took control at the San Siro in less than a minute, World Player of the Year Weah scoring almost straight from the kick-off for his fourth goal in four matches.
Not even the sending-off in the 67th minute of Croatian midfielder Zvonimir Boban for his second bookable offence could knock the Milan side out of their stride.
Down to 10 men, they still managed to move up a gear with Liberian Weah adding his second from 20 metres, then second-half substitute Baggio scoring with a superb goal direct from a free-kick.
City neighbours Internazionale, held 1-1 at Atalanta, were left to rue Felippo Inzaghi's equaliser five minutes from time.
Until Inzaghi's late blow, French international Youri Djorkaeff's 44th minute strike looked like lifting Inter to the top of the table for the first time since the 1990-91 season.
Instead arch-rivals AC Milan lead serie A with nine points from four matches, with Inter a point adrift.
European champions Juventus will go to the top if they beat Fiorentina in an evening match.
Parma, leaders at the start of the day, followed up their midweek elimination from the UEFA Cup with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Lazio at Rome's Olympic stadium.
Igor Protti, a prolific striker with Bari last season, opened the scoring in the 26th minute with his first goal since joining Lazio and Pierluigi Casiraghi added a second in the 61st.
A 65th minute header from Dino Baggio pulled one back and left Lazio to survive a tense finale for their first win of the season.
Like Inter, Roma and Udinese both conceded late equalisers to squander the chance to join Milan at the top.

At Reggio Emilia, Damiano Tommasi's sixth minute opener for Roma looked enough for three points until a defensive error gave Reggiana's Colombian Adolfo Valencia the chance to level the scores in the 78th minute.

At Udine, Russian Igor Shalimov celebrated his debut for Bologna by setting-up Carlo Nervo's 83rd minute equaliser as the visitors, newly promoted this season, recovered from two goals down to claim a point.

Udinese had looked set for their third successive victory after Giovanni Bia and German Oliver Bierhoff put them two up in the first 16 minutes but Giancarlo Marocchi's 37th minute volley sparked Bologna's fightback.
Bottom-of-the-table Verona claimed their first point of the season, twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Cagliari.
